summary: SCIM sync removed secondary email, blocking SSH key provisioning and CLI login
description:
Issue summary:
A recent SCIM sync run on 2026-03-10 inadvertently cleared the secondaryEmail attribute for ~28 internal accounts that have an existing mobile attribute. Those accounts could not complete the SSH key provisioning pipeline which requires a secondary email for verification, resulting in CLI login failures and blocked runbook access for affected engineers.

Impact:
- ~28 affected internal users (oncall and SRE) unable to provision SSH keys via the normal CLI flow.
- Runbooks that require live CLI access were delayed; a critical incident runbook had to use a bastion workaround for one case.
- No customer-facing service degradation observed.

Environment:
prod (us-east) identity sync job (scim-provisioner v1.7.2) triggered nightly reconciliation.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Take a user account with primaryEmail and secondaryEmail set and a mobile phone number in Okta.
2) Run the nightly SCIM full reconciliation against the identity-provisioner service.
3) Observe secondaryEmail is cleared in the downstream identity store after the sync.
4) Attempt SSH key provisioning via the CLI; verification step fails because secondary email is missing.

Observed logs/snippets:
- scim-provisioner logs (2026-03-10T02:12:47Z): "INFO reconcile:user U12345 - attributes delta: mobile:+1-XXX, secondaryEmail:-removed-"
- ssh-provisioner: "ERROR user U12345 - missing secondary_email for verification, aborting provisioning"
- Okta system audit: shows SCIM patch for attribute mapping alias 'contact.secondary' applied to multiple users with source app 'HRSync' at 02:11Z.

Initial hypothesis:
The SCIM attribute mapping that reconciles Okta profile -> identity store contains an erroneous override rule when mobile is present; the mapping program treats a blank patch target as a delete operation. A remapping change from HRSync last week likely introduced the regression.

Immediate workaround applied:
Support manually patched secondaryEmail for impacted users via identity-provisioner admin endpoint to unblock SSH provisioning. We ran the ssh-provisioner CLI re-provision flow and verified successful key issuance for 26/28 accounts; two accounts required additional manual verification (now cleared).

investigation_notes: Checked PR history: commit abcdef3 (2026-03-03) updated mapping rules to canonicalize phone numbers; accidentally re-used the same mapping object for 'contact' group leading to side-effect deletion.
Replayed nightly job in staging against anonymized data; reproduced deletion when mobile value exists and secondaryEmail is non-null (edge-case: serialization produced empty string).
Added unit test covering mapping when mobile present and secondaryEmail non-empty; failing prior to change, passing after guard fix.
Correlation with HRSync: HRSync introduced contact.phone_normalized attribute; scim-provisioner mapping code path didn't handle absence of contact.secondary target correctly.
Affected users list exported to /tmp/INT-864880-affected.csv and shared with SRE and Oncall.
resolution:
Workaround and fix status:
- Manual remediation: secondaryEmail restored for all 28 impacted accounts on 2026-03-10 and provisioning retried successfully.
- Hotfix: scim-provisioner deployed (v1.7.3) with guard against empty-string deletes for secondaryEmail and explicit no-op when source mapping missing. Deployed to canary 2026-03-11 and promoted to prod us-east 2026-03-13.
- Root cause: faulty attribute mapping reuse in commit abcdef3 which caused an empty-string patch to be interpreted as delete for secondaryEmail when mobile normalization occurred.
- Post-incident actions: add mapping unit tests, add a schema assertion to scim-provisioner to reject delete patches for secondaryEmail without explicit intent, and update the SCIM runbook to include verification step post-reconciliation.

Follow-ups:
- Owner: Julian Park to file PR for unit tests and schema assertion (PR linked above).
- Runbook owner: Priya Nambiar to update SCIM reconciliation checklist.
- Security review: Tomas Reed to sign off on audit entry by 2026-03-17.
